problem: If $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are polynomials of degree $5$ and $9$, respectively, what is the degree of $P-Q?$

feedback.problem: If $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are polynomials of degree $2$ and $7$, respectively, what is the degree of $P-Q?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $P$ is a polynomial of degree $2,$ the leading term contains an ${x}^{2}.$

Since $Q$ is a polynomial of degree $7,$ the leading term contains an ${x}^{7}.$

In $P-Q,$ the highest-order term still contains an ${x}^{7}.$ No ${x}^{7}$ term in $P$ could possibly cancel out the ${x}^{7}$ term in $Q.$

Therefore, the degree of $P-Q$ must be $7.$
